scope: National freshwater spatial-framework source review; not a fish checklist or occurrence review.

dataset.title: National-scale geodatabase of catchment characteristics in the Philippines for river management applications
dataset.citation: Boothroyd, R. J., Williams, R. D., Hoey, T. B., et al. (2023). PLOS ONE 18(3): e0281933. DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0281933. Data Collection DOI: 10.5525/gla.researchdata.1396.
dataset.repository: University of Glasgow Enlighten Research Data
dataset.licenseEvidence: The official data repository labels each downloaded file CC BY 4.0.

relatedNationalHydrologyLead.paperLicense: CC BY 3.0 for the paper only
relatedNationalHydrologyLead.note: A 2023 primary paper describes the PHD inventory as 770 principal basins; it distinguishes this broader project lead from the 128-catchment CC BY 4.0 dataset actually downloaded and checked here.
relatedNationalHydrologyLead.dataAccess: Official LiPAD manual-request route identified; specific 770-basin layer, current access, fee, eligibility and data license remain unverified.

decision.use: Use as an internal, nationwide river-catchment discovery and scope-planning aid. Reconcile catchments with official regional and administrative geometry before assigning them to rollout regions.
decision.lakeCoverage: Not a standalone lake inventory. Large lakes and reservoirs are represented as flat areas in the underlying DEM workflow; the source paper notes unquantified effects for catchments including Marikina-Pasig, Pansipit and Agno.
limitations: Only 128 catchments larger than 250 km2 are included; smaller river systems are out of scope.
The dataset describes catchment and stream-network morphology, not fish presence, catch dates, habitat suitability or fishing access.
Catchment geometry is hydrological, not a legal marine boundary or administrative boundary.
The catchment polygons have not been overlaid with the project's 18-region registry.
No source geometry or derived map is copied into public app assets by this review.
next: Verify the access path and item-specific terms for the broader 770-basin PHD data before acquisition.
Overlay the 128 hydrological polygons against a properly licensed official administrative geometry source.
Use basin names as a freshwater source-search frame, then review site-specific fish evidence separately.
Continue lake and reservoir inventory from independent lake/waterbody sources; do not infer lakes from river catchment geometry.

accessReview.portalStatus: The LiPAD site says the portal is under maintenance and directs data requests to two Google Forms.
accessReview.category: Hydrological Datasets is listed in the portal resource-map categories; the public page does not identify a specific 770-basin PHD layer or expose its license.
accessReview.requestRoute: Complete the requester registration form and the separate LiDAR Data Request form. The page says resource maps are available by manual request.
statedDocuments: Proof of consultancy when requesting on behalf of another organization
accessReview.wholeCountryHandling: For a large request such as the whole country, the portal instructs requesters to contact the Business Development Officer.
accessReview.costAndEligibility: No fee, eligibility decision, exact 770-basin dataset availability, or dataset license was confirmed.
